# Warm-up

---

::: {.question}
## What *initiates* the action potential?

- A. Rapid influx of K+ ions that makes the membrane potential more negative.
- B. Rapid outflow of A- ions that makes the membrane potential more negative.
- C. Input depolarizes (makes positive) the cell to the threshold voltage (~55 mv).
:::

::: {.fragment}
::: {.answer}
- ~~A. Rapid influx of K+ ions that makes the membrane potential more negative.~~
- ~~B. Rapid outflow of A- ions that makes the membrane potential more negative.~~
- **C. Input depolarizes (makes positive) the cell to the threshold voltage (~55 mv).**
:::
:::

---

::: {.question}
## The rising (depolarization) phase of the action potential occurs due to

- A. Opening of voltage-gated Na+ channels and Na+ inflow
- B. Opening of voltage-gated K+ channels and K+ outflow
- C. Closing of voltage-gated Na+ channels that stops rapid Na+ inflow
:::

::: {.fragment}
::: {.answer}
- **A. Opening of voltage-gated Na+ channels and rapid Na+ inflow**
- ~~B. Opening of voltage-gated K+ channels and rapid K+ outflow~~
- ~~C. Closing of voltage-gated Na+ channels that stops rapid Na+ inflow~~
:::
:::

---

::: {.question}
## The *peak* of the action potential occurs due to

- A. Opening of voltage-gated Na+ channels and Na+ inflow
- B. Opening of voltage-gated K+ channels and K+ outflow
- C. Closing of voltage-gated Na+ channels that stops rapid Na+ inflow
:::

::: {.fragment}
::: {.answer}
- ~~A. Opening of voltage-gated Na+ channels and rapid Na+ inflow~~
- ~~B. Opening of voltage-gated K+ channels and rapid K+ outflow~~
- **C. Closing of voltage-gated Na+ channels that stops rapid Na+ inflow**
:::
:::

---

::: {.question}
## The falling (repolarization) phase of the action potential occurs due to

- A. Opening of voltage-gated Na+ channels and Na+ inflow
- B. Opening of voltage-gated K+ channels and K+ outflow
- C. Closing of voltage-gated Na+ channels that stops rapid Na+ inflow
:::

::: {.fragment}
::: {.answer}
- ~~A. Opening of voltage-gated Na+ channels and rapid Na+ inflow~~
- **B. Opening of voltage-gated K+ channels and rapid K+ outflow**
- ~~C. Closing of voltage-gated Na+ channels that stops rapid Na+ inflow~~
:::
:::

## Key facts

::: {.incremental}
- Na/K pump creates concentration gradients
  - [Na+] outside >> inside $\rightarrow$ Na+ flows in
  - [K+] inside >> outside $\rightarrow$ K+ flows out
- Ion channels accelerate/slow ion flow
  - Open ion channel: Accelerate flow
  - Close ion channel: Slow flow

:::

## Key facts

::: {.incremental}
- Membrane potential magnitude & sign accelerates/slows ion flow
  - More - $\rightarrow$ attracts + charges
  - More + $\rightarrow$ repels + charges
- Ion flow changes membrane potential
  - Na+ inflow $\rightarrow$ membrane potential (voltage) more +
  - K+ outflow $\rightarrow$ membrane potential (voltage) more -
:::

## Why should I care?

- Action potentials are the language of thought

# Neurophysiology III

## Propagation

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=50%}
- Unmyelinated axons
  - Each segment "excites" the next
:::
::: {.column width=50%}
![@Wikipedia-contributors2025-xk](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/4/48/Saltatory_Conduction.gif){fig-align="right"}
:::
::::

## Propagation

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=50%}
- Myelinated axon
  + AP "jumps" between *Nodes of Ranvier*
  + voltage-gated $Na^+$, $K^+$ channels exposed
  + current flows through/down myelinated segments
:::
::: {.column width=50%}
![@Wikipedia-contributors2025-xk](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/4/48/Saltatory_Conduction.gif){fig-align="right"}
:::
::::

## Nodes of Ranvier

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=50%}
- *Regenerate* action potential
- $Na^+$ and $K^+$ channels exposed to extracellular environment
- Between Nodes of Ranvier, ions can't move out, so move along
:::
::: {.column width=50%}
![@Wikipedia-contributors2025-np](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/3/3b/Nodes_of_Ranvier.png){fig-align="right"}
:::
::::

## Nodes of Ranvier

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=50%}
- Action potentials faster & more reliable for a given axon diameter
:::
::: {.column width=50%}
![@Wikipedia-contributors2025-np](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/3/3b/Nodes_of_Ranvier.png){fig-align="right"}
:::
::::

## Why does AP flow in one direction, away from soma?

+ Soma does not have (many) voltage-gated Na+ channels.
+ Soma is not myelinated.
+ Refractory periods mean polarization works only in one direction.

## Why does AP flow in one direction, away from soma?

+ **Soma does not have (many) voltage-gated Na+ channels.**
+ Soma is not myelinated.
+ **Refractory periods mean polarization works only in one direction.**

## How fast are APs?

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=50%}
- Axons carry information at different rates
    - Ticker myelin -> faster
    - Larger diameter axon -> faster
- Somatosensory information faster than pain (nociception)
:::
::: {.column width=50%}
![@Wikipedia-contributors2025-xk](../include/img/sensory-fiber-speeds.png)
:::
::::

---

![@Wikipedia-contributors2025-xk](../include/img/sensory-fiber-speeds.png)

---

```{r}
#| label: fig-speed-myelin-axon-diameter
#| fig-cap: "Myelin and axon diameter vs. action potential speed. Data from @Wikipedia-contributors2025-xk."
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

ap <- readr::read_csv("../include/csv/action-potential-speeds.csv",
                      show_col_types = FALSE)

ap |>
  mutate(
    x = (diameter_min + diameter_max) / 2,
    y = (velocity_min + velocity_max) / 2
  ) |>
  ggplot() +
  aes(
    x = x,
    y = y,
    xmin = diameter_min,
    xmax = diameter_max,
    ymin = velocity_min,
    ymax = velocity_max,
    color = myelin
  ) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = velocity_min, ymax = velocity_max),
    orientation = "x",
    width = 0.2
  ) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = velocity_min, ymax = velocity_max),
    orientation = "y",
    width = 0.2
  ) +
  xlab("m/s") +
  ylab("diameter microns") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```


## Information processing

- Action potential amplitudes don't vary (much)
    + All or none (fire or don't fire)
    + $Na^+$/$K^+$ pumps working all the time
    + $[K^+]$ & $[Na^+]$ don't vary much, so
    + $V_{K^+}$ & $V_{Na^+}$ don't vary much
    
## Information processing

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=50%}
- Action potential *frequency* and *timing* vary
  + Rate vs. timing codes
  + Neurons use both
- Action potentials analogous to 1s and 0s used as bits of information in digital computers
:::
::: {.column width=50%}
![@eyherabide_bursts_2009](http://www.frontiersin.org/files/Articles/490/fnins-03-002/image_n/fnins-03-002-g001.gif)
:::
::::

# Anatomy: Spinal cord & PNS

## Spinal cord

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=50%}
- Rostral/Caudal axis
    - Spinal column w/ vertebrae
    - Cervical (8), thoracic (12), lumbar (5), sacral (5), coccygeal (1)
    - Spinal segments & 31 nerve pairs 
    - Cauda equina
:::
::: {.column width=50%}
![By Sheryl Tan, Faull L, Curtis A - The Anatomical record, CC BY 4.0, https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=152594765](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/72/Spinal_cord_details.jpg/1920px-Spinal_cord_details.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=imageinfo&utm_content=thumbnail){width="75%"}
:::
::::

## Spinal cord

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=50%}
- Nerves map to specific regions of the body
- [Dermatomes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dermatome_(anatomy))
:::
::: {.column width=50%}
![By Grant, John Charles Boileau - An atlas of anatomy, / by regions 1962, Public Domain, https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=30017222](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/93/Grant_1962_663.png/1920px-Grant_1962_663.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=imageinfo&utm_content=thumbnail){#fig-dermatomes width="65%"}
:::
::::

## Spinal cord

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=50%}
- Dorsal/Ventral
  + Dorsal root (sensory)
  + Ventral root (mostly motor)
- Grey (interior) vs. white matter (exterior)
:::
::: {.column width=50%}
![https://www.britannica.com/science/spinal-cord](https://cdn.britannica.com/75/2975-050-0D5D3A36/views-cross-section-Photograph-cord-segment-drawing.jpg?w=400&h=300&c=crop){#fig-spinal-cord-cross-section}
:::
::::

## Spinal cord

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=50%}
- Afferent (input/sensory) and efferent (output/motor) tracts
:::
::: {.column width=50%}
![https://med.libretexts.org/Sandboxes/admin/Introduction_to_Neuroscience_%28Hedges%29/04%3A_Nervous_System_Organization/4.06%3A_Spinal_Cord_Structure](https://med.libretexts.org/@api/deki/files/43083/Nerve-Classifications-1024x760.png?revision=1){#fig-spinal-cord-cross-section}
:::
::::

## Organization of the PNS  

- Somatic division
    - Voluntary sensory & motor function
- Autonomic division
    - Involuntary sensory & motor function
- Cranial nerves
- Spinal nerves

## Cranial nerves

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=50%}
- Sensory & motor functions of the cranium (head) and neck
- Afferents (input/sensory), efferents (output/motor), or mixed/both
  - On Old Olympus' Towering Top...
  - Some Say Marry Money...
:::
::: {.column width=50%}
![Encyclopedia Britannica](https://cdn.britannica.com/44/54244-004-892C5169/nerves-pairs-muscles-region-head-sense-organs.jpg)
:::
::::

## Cranial nerves

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=50%}
- Innervate head and neck
- Olfactory (I), optic (II), (VIII) auditory,
vagus (X), etc. 
:::
::: {.column width=50%}
![Encyclopedia Britannica](https://cdn.britannica.com/44/54244-004-892C5169/nerves-pairs-muscles-region-head-sense-organs.jpg)
:::
::::

## Autonomic nervous system (ANS) 

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=50%}
- CNS & PNS components
- Controls "vegetative functions""
    + Limited voluntary control
- Two divisions
    + Sympathetic
    + Parasympathetic
:::
::: {.column width=50%}
![](http://humanphysiology.academy/Neurosciences%202015/Images/2/NEU_autonomic_nervous_system%20Merck%20Manuals.gif){#fig-ans width="70%"}
:::
::::

## Sympathetic division 

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=50%}
- Prepares body for action
- "Fight or flight"
- Spinal cord
    + ganglion chain along spinal column to end organs
:::
::: {.column width=50%}
![](http://humanphysiology.academy/Neurosciences%202015/Images/2/NEU_autonomic_nervous_system%20Merck%20Manuals.gif){#fig-symp width="70%" fig-align="right"}
:::
::::

## Sympathetic division

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=50%}
- Neurotransmitters
    + Preganglionic: Acetylcholine (ACh) 
    + Post: Norepinephrine (NE)
:::
::: {.column width=50%}
![](http://humanphysiology.academy/Neurosciences%202015/Images/2/NEU_autonomic_nervous_system%20Merck%20Manuals.gif){#fig-symp-2 width="70%" fig-align="right"}
:::
::::

## Parasympathetic division 

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=50%}
- Para -> "around"
- Restorative function
- "Rest & digest"
- Spinal cord -> ganglia near end organs -> end organ
    + Neurotransmitter: Acetylcholine (ACh)
:::
::: {.column width=50%}
![](http://humanphysiology.academy/Neurosciences%202015/Images/2/NEU_autonomic_nervous_system%20Merck%20Manuals.gif){#fig-parasymp width="70%" fig-align="right"}
:::
::::
